summary: Read-only review complete: 3 material findings. No edits, builds, tests, or network access.

findings.title: Splitting password change and session revocation leaves compromised sessions valid indefinitely
findings.detail: account.ts:382-394 currently changes the password and revokes other sessions atomically. The proposed second transaction can fail or never start after the password transaction commits. resolveCustomer does not compare session authentication against security_epoch, so those sessions remain usable until expiration or another revocation; the window is not bounded to milliseconds.
findings.fix: | Signed-in password change (`account.ts`) | `me()` (renewal may lock session) → verify → customer update → delete other sessions | **restructured**: verify the password and compute the replacement hash outside the mutation transaction using an explicitly non-renewing credential read. In one mutation transaction: customer `FOR UPDATE` → non-renewing live-session re-read → hash snapshot re-check (`password_hash` unchanged since verification, else 409 `CREDENTIAL_CHANGED`) → password update and trigger-driven epoch bump → delete C/P/G/M → delete every other session for this customer and store. Keep the calling session. Commit the password change, artifact invalidation and session revocation atomically; any failure rolls back all three. Apply the resolver restructuring in the following row before retaining this customer-to-session order. Add a failure-injection test through the real password-change route proving that failure during session revocation leaves the password, epoch and artifacts unchanged. |

findings.title: The retained renewal paths still contradict the claimed lock discipline
findings.detail: Profile update and address creation retain session locks from resolveCustomer before updating or referencing the customer. Password reset, email-change consumption and erasure retain the customer lock before deleting sessions. A profile transaction can hold session S and wait for customer C while reset holds C and waits to delete S. The same reverse order exists in loyalty.ts birthday updates and SheerID resolver callers, which the table omits. Testing only new transactions against existing rows does not exercise these retained cycles.
findings.fix: | Customer session resolution and subsequent business mutations (`auth/session.ts` and its callers, including profile/address operations in `account.ts`, birthday updates in `loyalty.ts`, and verification operations in `sheerid.ts`) | `resolveCustomer()` can renew and lock a session before a later customer update or customer-FK check; reset, email-change consumption and erasure acquire the customer before deleting sessions | **restructured**: add an explicit non-renewing mode to `resolveCustomer` and its wrappers; the existing `forceRenew = false` does not disable automatic renewal. Business transactions use non-renewing resolution and revalidate the live session inside their own transaction. Preserve automatic renewal in a separate resolver transaction that commits before business locks are acquired; do not open that transaction from inside another transaction. Keep existing commerce-lock ordering before customer locks. Add deterministic tests through the real profile, address, birthday and SheerID paths against password reset, signed-in password change, email-change consumption and erasure, with renewal eligible and both lock interleavings; verify that none deadlocks. |

findings.title: Native step-up can stamp a stale proof with the current epoch
findings.detail: The proposed native step-up checks only the verified hash/secret snapshot before writing the current epoch. getAdminCredentialsById currently returns no epoch. In the supported plaintext-TOTP configuration, disable followed by re-enable with the same secret restores the identical snapshot while advancing security_epoch twice. If both mutations keep the calling session, an in-flight step-up verified before the cycle can resume afterward and mint a usable step-up at the new epoch. Comparing epochs only after issuance does not detect this.
findings.fix: | Native admin step-up (`admin-system.ts` → `admin-session.ts:232`) | session update, no owner lock | **restructured**: read `security_epoch`, `password_hash` and the stored TOTP version together in `getAdminCredentialsById` before verifying the password and second factor. Carry that verified snapshot into the mutation transaction: `admin_user` `FOR UPDATE` → require both the captured epoch and the hash/TOTP snapshot to equal the locked row, otherwise reject with 409 `CREDENTIAL_CHANGED` → calling session `FOR UPDATE` with owner, expiry and idle revalidation → write `step_up_at` and the captured, still-current `step_up_epoch`. Never assign the current epoch to proof obtained under a different epoch. Add a deterministic real-route test that pauses native step-up after credential verification, disables and re-enables the same plaintext TOTP secret while keeping the calling session, then resumes step-up and proves that no usable step-up is written. |
